name: Bash

content:
Releases are cut by pushing a git tag, and CI does the rest.

1. Pick the next version in the form `vYYYY.MM.N`. For example, `v2026.09.2` is the second release of September 2026. Since today is 2026-10-01, the first release this month would be `v2026.10.1`.
2. Create the tag on `main` and push it, for example `git tag v2026.10.1 && git push origin v2026.10.1`.
3. CI builds and publishes. Never publish by hand.

This comes from a shared project convention stored in EngramDB. I couldn't find a release doc, CI workflow or existing tags in the repo to confirm it. The repo has no `.github/workflows` directory, so I don't know where CI is configured. Check the last `N` used for the current month before choosing the next one.
